name: Texas Wolfberry

facts.where: Coastal flats and dry South Texas

caution: This is the nightshade family: eat ONLY the ripe red berries of correctly identified wolfberry, never leaves or unripe fruit, and be certain of the plant. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A wild cousin of the cultivated goji, with small red berries on a spiny succulent-leaved shrub. Nightshade family means positive ID matters more than usual.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The ripe berries are mildly sweet-savory and were a traditional food, eaten fresh or dried.
